events.title: Washington Signs the Postal Service Act
events.description: President George Washington signed the Postal Service Act, which created the United States Post Office Department. The law set up a national system for delivering mail across the young republic.
events.significance: It laid the groundwork for a national postal network. That network helped link distant communities and spread news and ideas in the early United States.

events.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art Opens in New York City
events.description: The Metropolitan Museum of Art opened its doors in New York City. It began as an ambitious project to bring art and art education to the American public.
events.significance: The Met grew into one of the largest and most visited art museums in the world.

events.title: Congress Proposes the 21st Amendment
events.description: The United States Congress proposed the 21st Amendment to the Constitution. It was sent to the states for ratification, with the aim of ending national Prohibition.
events.significance: The amendment was later ratified and repealed the 18th Amendment. It is the only constitutional amendment ever to repeal another.

events.title: John Glenn Orbits the Earth
events.description: Aboard the Friendship 7 capsule, launched by an Atlas rocket, John Glenn became the first American to orbit the Earth. He completed three orbits before splashing down in the Atlantic Ocean.
events.significance: Glenn's flight was a major milestone in the Space Race. It boosted American confidence and showed that the United States could put humans into orbit.
